verdict.rationale: Pinecone documents dense-vector semantic search, including ranking by `dense_vector` in `score_by`. A community comment notes it offered HNSW (approximate nearest-neighbor) indexing, so the core similarity search is evidenced. However, nothing in the pack documents configurable distance metrics such as cosine, euclidean or dot product, which is half of the story. Missing for 10: documentation of selectable distance metrics, first-party documentation of the ANN algorithm and its tuning, hands-on corroboration of search quality.

support.subject: As a developer, I can run approximate nearest-neighbor similarity search over embeddings with configurable distance metrics

citations.quote: When you search, you rank results via `score_by`: `text` (BM25), `query_string` (Lucene), `dense_vector`, or `sparse_vector`.
A single index can serve full-text search (BM25 with Lucene queries), semantic search, and sparse-vector search together
There was a long time that pgvector only had basic similarity algorithms and not HNSW but pinecone did.
